desc: Ideation: establish that only values ≤ threshold can have edges; divisor-of-L unioning via sieve anchors is correct and covers non-divisor edges (lcm(a,b)=L₀ ≤ threshold means both divide L₀, unioned at L₀); complexity O(threshold·H(threshold)) ≈ 2.4e6.
Mentally verify anchor approach on Example 1 ([2,4,8,3,9], t=5 → 4) and Example 2 ([2,4,8,3,9,12], t=10 → 2) — both trace correctly.
Implement DSU (parent, rank arrays of size threshold+1) with path compression and union by rank.
Build presence array from nums; count elements > threshold as isolated.
Sieve loop: for each present v ≤ threshold, for L in range(v, threshold+1, v): if anchor[L] set → union(v, anchor[L]); else anchor[L] = v.
Count distinct roots via find() over present values ≤ threshold; add count of values > threshold.
Final code in starter class with `from typing import List`; sanity-check edge cases (threshold=1, single element, value exactly equal to threshold, non-divisor edge like [6,10] t=15 → 1 component).
